exercises.heading: Section 6.3 Exercises

problem.paragraph: True or False? If vector field F is conservative on the open and connected region D, then line integrals of F are path independent on D, regardless of the shape of D.

solution.paragraph: True

problem.paragraph: True or False? Function $$\mathbf{ \text{r} }(t) = \mathbf{ \text{a} } + t\left( {\mathbf{ \text{b} } - \mathbf{ \text{a} }} \right),$$ where $$0 \leq t \leq 1,$$ parameterizes the straight-line segment from $$\mathbf{ \text{a} } \text{to} \mathbf{ \text{b} }.$$

True or False? Vector field $$\mathbf{ \text{F} }\left( {x,y,z} \right) = \left( {y \sin z} \right)\mathbf{ \text{i} } + \left( {x \sin z} \right)\mathbf{ \text{j} } + \left( {xy \cos z} \right)\mathbf{ \text{k} }$$ is conservative.

solution.paragraph: True

problem.paragraph: True or False? Vector field $$\mathbf{ \text{F} }\left( {x,y,z} \right) = y\mathbf{ \text{i} } + \left( {x + z} \right)\mathbf{ \text{j} } - y\mathbf{ \text{k} }$$ is conservative.

Verify the Fundamental Theorem of Line Integrals for $$\int_{C}{\mathbf{ \text{F} } \cdot d\mathbf{ \text{r} }}$$ by computing the integral using a parameterization and, separately, by finding a potential function for the case when $$\mathbf{ \text{F} }\left( {x,y} \right) = \left( {2x + 2y} \right)\mathbf{ \text{i} } + \left( {2x + 2y} \right)\mathbf{ \text{j} }$$ and C is a portion of circle $$x^{2} + y^{2} = 25$$ oriented counterclockwise from (5, 0) to (3, 4).

solution.paragraph: $$\int C F \cdot d r = 24 \int C F \cdot d r = 24$$

problem.paragraph: [T] Find $${\int_{C}^{}{\mathbf{ \text{F} } \cdot d\mathbf{ \text{r} }}},$$ where $$\mathbf{ \text{F} }(x,y) = \left( {ye^{xy} + \cos x} \right)\mathbf{ \text{i} } + \left( {xe^{xy} + \frac{1}{y^{2} + 1}} \right)\mathbf{ \text{j} }$$ and C is a portion of curve $$y = \sin x$$ from $$x = 0$$ to $$x = \frac{\pi}{2}.$$

[T] Evaluate line integral $${\int_{C}^{}{\mathbf{ \text{F} } \cdot d\mathbf{ \text{r} }}},$$ where $$\mathbf{ \text{F} }(x,y) = \left( {e^{x}\sin y - y} \right)\mathbf{ \text{i} } + \left( {e^{x}\cos y - x - 2} \right)\mathbf{ \text{j} },$$ and C is the path given by $$\mathbf{r}(t) = \left\lbrack {t^{3}\sin \frac{\pi t}{2}} \right\rbrack\mathbf{ \text{i} } - \left\lbrack {\frac{\pi}{2}\cos \left( {\frac{\pi t}{2} + \frac{\pi}{2}} \right)} \right\rbrack\mathbf{ \text{j} }$$ for $$0 \leq t \leq 1.$$

solution.paragraph: $$\int C F \cdot d r = e - 3 \pi 2 \int C F \cdot d r = e - 3 \pi 2$$

exercises.paragraph: For the following exercises, determine whether the vector field is conservative and, if it is, find the potential function.

problem.paragraph: $$\mathbf{ \text{F} }(x,y) = 2xy^{3}\mathbf{ \text{i} } + 3y^{2}x^{2}\mathbf{ \text{j} }$$
$$\mathbf{ \text{F} }(x,y) = \left( {-y + e^{x}\sin y} \right)\mathbf{ \text{i} } + \left\lbrack {\left( {x + 2} \right)e^{x}\cos y} \right\rbrack\mathbf{ \text{j} }$$

solution.paragraph: Not conservative

problem.paragraph: $$\mathbf{ \text{F} }(x,y) = \left( {e^{2x}\sin y} \right)\mathbf{ \text{i} } + \left\lbrack {e^{2x}\cos y} \right\rbrack\mathbf{ \text{j} }$$
$$\mathbf{ \text{F} }(x,y) = (6x + 5y)\mathbf{ \text{i} } + (5x + 4y)\mathbf{ \text{j} }$$

solution.paragraph: Conservative, $$f(x,y)=3x2+5xy+2y2f(x,y)=3x2+5xy+2y2$$

problem.paragraph: $$\mathbf{ \text{F} }(x,y) = \left\lbrack {2x \cos (y) - y \cos (x)} \right\rbrack\mathbf{ \text{i} } + \left\lbrack {-x^{2}\sin (y) - \sin (x)} \right\rbrack\mathbf{ \text{j} }$$
$$\mathbf{ \text{F} }(x,y) = \left\lbrack {ye^{x} + \sin (y)} \right\rbrack\mathbf{ \text{i} } + \left\lbrack {e^{x} + x \cos (y)} \right\rbrack\mathbf{ \text{j} }$$

solution.paragraph: Conservative, $$f(x,y)=yex+xsin(y)f(x,y)=yex+xsin(y)$$

exercises.paragraph: For the following exercises, evaluate the line integrals using the Fundamental Theorem of Line Integrals.

problem.paragraph: $${\int_{C}{(y\mathbf{ \text{i} } + x\mathbf{ \text{j} }) \cdot d\mathbf{ \text{r} }}},$$ where C is any path from (0, 0) to (2, 4)
$${\int_{C}{(2ydx + 2xdy)}},$$ where C is the line segment from (0, 0) to (4, 4)

solution.paragraph: $$\int C ( 2 y d x + 2 x d y ) = 32 \int C ( 2 y d x + 2 x d y ) = 32$$

problem.paragraph: [T] $${\int_{C}{\left\lbrack {\arctan \frac{y}{x} - \frac{xy}{x^{2} + y^{2}}} \right\rbrack dx + \left\lbrack {\frac{x^{2}}{x^{2} + y^{2}} + e^{-y}(1 - y)} \right\rbrack dy}},$$ where C is any smooth curve from (1, 1) to $$\left( {-1,2} \right)$$
Find the conservative vector field for the potential function

exercises.paragraph: For the following exercises, determine whether the vector field is conservative and, if so, find a potential function.

problem.paragraph: $$\mathbf{ \text{F} }(x,y) = \left( {12xy} \right)\mathbf{ \text{i} } + 6\left( {x^{2} + y^{2}} \right)\mathbf{ \text{j} }$$
$$\mathbf{ \text{F} }(x,y) = \left( {e^{x}\cos y} \right)\mathbf{ \text{i} } + 6\left( {e^{x}\sin y} \right)\mathbf{ \text{j} }$$

solution.paragraph: F is not conservative.

problem.paragraph: $$\mathbf{ \text{F} }(x,y) = \left( {2xye^{x^{2}y}} \right)\mathbf{ \text{i} } + \left( {x^{2}e^{x^{2}y}} \right)\mathbf{ \text{j} }$$
$$\mathbf{ \text{F} }(x,y, z) = \left( {ye^{z}} \right)\mathbf{ \text{i} } + \left( {xe^{z}} \right)\mathbf{ \text{j} } + \left( {xye^{z}} \right)\mathbf{ \text{k} }$$

solution.paragraph: F is conservative and a potential function is $$f(x,y,z)=xyez.f(x,y,z)=xyez.$$

problem.paragraph: $$\mathbf{ \text{F} }(x,y, z) = \left( {\sin y} \right)\mathbf{ \text{i} } - \left( {x \cos y} \right)\mathbf{ \text{j} } + \mathbf{ \text{k} }$$
$$\mathbf{ \text{F} }(x,y, z) = \left( {-\frac{1}{y}} \right)\mathbf{ \text{i} } + \left( \frac{x}{y^{2}} \right)\mathbf{ \text{j} } + \left( {2z - 1} \right)\mathbf{ \text{k} }$$

solution.paragraph: F is conservative and a potential function is $$f(x,y,z)=z2-z-xy.f(x,y,z)=z2-z-xy.$$

problem.paragraph: $$\mathbf{ \text{F} }(x,y,z) = 3z^{2}\mathbf{ \text{i} } - \cos y\mathbf{ \text{j} } + 2xz\mathbf{ \text{k} }$$
$$\mathbf{ \text{F} }(x,y, z) = \left( {2xy} \right)\mathbf{ \text{i} } + \left( {x^{2} + 2yz} \right)\mathbf{ \text{j} } + y^{2}\mathbf{ \text{k} }$$

solution.paragraph: F is conservative and a potential function is $$f(x,y,z)=x2y+y2z.f(x,y,z)=x2y+y2z.$$

problem.paragraph: $$\mathbf{ \text{F} }\left( {x,y} \right) = \left( 4{e^{x}\cos y} \right)\mathbf{ \text{i} }-\left( 4{e^{x}\sin y} \right)\mathbf{ \text{j} }$$
$$\mathbf{ \text{F} }\left( {x,y} \right) = \left( {ye^{x^{2}}} \right)\mathbf{ \text{i} } + \left( {x^{2}e^{y^{2}}} \right)\mathbf{ \text{j} }$$

solution.paragraph: F is conservative and a potential function is $$f(x,y)=ex2yf(x,y)=ex2y$$

exercises.paragraph: For the following exercises, evaluate the integral using the Fundamental Theorem of Line Integrals.

problem.paragraph: Evaluate $${\int_{C}{\nabla f \cdot d\mathbf{ \text{r} }}},$$ where $$f(x,y, z) = \cos (\pi x) + \sin (\pi y) - xyz$$ and C is any path that starts at $$\left( {1,\frac{1}{2},2} \right)$$ and ends at $$\left( {2,1,-1} \right).$$
[T] Evaluate $${\int_{C}{\nabla f \cdot d\mathbf{ \text{r} }}},$$ where $$f(x,y) = xy + e^{x}$$ and C is a straight line from $$\left( {0,0} \right)$$ to $$\left( {2,1} \right).$$

solution.paragraph: $$\int C F \cdot d r = e 2 + 1 \int C F \cdot d r = e 2 + 1$$

problem.paragraph: [T] Evaluate $${\int_{C}{\nabla f \cdot d\mathbf{ \text{r} }}},$$ where $$f(x,y) = x^{2}y - x$$ and C is any path in a plane from (1, 2) to (3, 2).
Evaluate $${\int_{C}{\nabla f \cdot d\mathbf{ \text{r} }}},$$ where $$f(x,y, z) = xyz^{2} - yz$$ and C has initial point (1, 2, 3) and terminal point (3, 5, 1).

solution.paragraph: $$\int C F \cdot d r = -2 \int C F \cdot d r = -2$$

exercises.paragraph: For the following exercises, let $$\mathbf{ \text{F} }(x,y) = 2xy^{2}\mathbf{ \text{i} } + \left( {2yx^{2} + 2y} \right)\mathbf{ \text{j} }$$ and $$\mathbf{G}(x,y) = (y + x)\mathbf{ \text{i} } + (y - x)\mathbf{ \text{j} },$$ and let C1 be the curve consisting of the circle of radius 2, centered at the origin and oriented counterclockwise, and C2 be the curve consisting of a line segment from (0, 0) to (1, 1) followed by a line segment from (1, 1) to (3, 1).

problem.paragraph: Calculate the line integral of F over C1.
Calculate the line integral of G over C1.

solution.paragraph: $$\int C 1 G \cdot d r = -8 \pi \int C 1 G \cdot d r = -8 \pi$$

problem.paragraph: Calculate the line integral of F over C2.
Calculate the line integral of G over C2.

solution.paragraph: $$\int C 2 G \cdot d r = 7 \int C 2 G \cdot d r = 7$$

problem.paragraph: [T] Let $$\mathbf{ \text{F} }(x,y,z) = x^{2}\mathbf{ \text{i} } + z \sin (yz)\mathbf{ \text{j} } + y \sin (yz)\mathbf{ \text{k} }.$$ Calculate $${\int_{C}{\mathbf{ \text{F} } \cdot dr}},$$ where C is a path from $$A = (0,0,1)$$ to $$B = (3,1,2).$$

[T] Find line integral $$\int_{C}{\mathbf{ \text{F} } \cdot dr}$$ of vector field $$\mathbf{ \text{F} }(x,y,z) = 3x^{2}z\mathbf{ \text{i} } + z^{2}\mathbf{ \text{j} } + \left( {x^{3} + 2yz} \right)\mathbf{ \text{k} }$$ along curve C parameterized by $$\mathbf{r}(t) = \left( \frac{\ln t}{\ln 2} \right)\mathbf{ \text{i} } + t^{3/2}\mathbf{ \text{j} } + t \cos {\left( {\pi t} \right)\mathbf{k}}, 1 \leq t \leq 4.$$

solution.paragraph: $$\int C F \cdot d r = 159 \int C F \cdot d r = 159$$

exercises.paragraph: For the following exercises, show that the following vector fields are conservative by using a computer. Calculate $$\int_{C}{\mathbf{ \text{F} } \cdot d\mathbf{ \text{r} }}$$ for the given curve.

problem.paragraph: $$\mathbf{ \text{F} } = \left( {xy^{2} + 3x^{2}y} \right)\mathbf{ \text{i} } + \left( {x + y} \right)x^{2}\mathbf{ \text{j} };$$ C is the curve consisting of line segments from $$(1,1)$$ to $$(0,2)$$ to $$(3,0).$$

$$\mathbf{ \text{F} } = \frac{2x}{y^{2} + 1}\mathbf{ \text{i} } - \frac{2y\left( {x^{2} + 1} \right)}{\left( {y^{2} + 1} \right)^{2}}\mathbf{ \text{j} };$$ C is parameterized by $$x = t^{3} - 1,y = t^{6} - t,0 \leq t \leq 1.$$

solution.paragraph: $$\int C F \cdot d r = -1 \int C F \cdot d r = -1$$

problem.paragraph: [T] $$\mathbf{ \text{F} } = \left\lbrack {\cos \left( {xy^{2}} \right) - xy^{2}\sin \left( {xy^{2}} \right)} \right\rbrack\mathbf{ \text{i} } - 2x^{2}y \sin \left( {xy^{2}} \right)\mathbf{ \text{j} };$$ C is curve $${\mathbf{r}(t) = {< {e^{t},e^{t + 1}} >}},-1 \leq t \leq 0.$$

The mass of Earth is approximately $$6 \times 10^{27} \text{g}$$ and that of the Sun is 330,000 times as much. The gravitational constant is $$6.7 \times 10^{-8}{ \text{cm} ^{3}/{\left( \text{s} ^{2} \cdot \text{g} \right).}}$$ The distance of Earth from the Sun is about $$1.5 \times 10^{12} \text{cm} .$$ Compute, approximately, the work necessary to increase the distance of Earth from the Sun by $$1 \text{cm} .$$

solution.paragraph: $$4 \times 10 29 erg 4 \times 10 29 erg$$

problem.paragraph: [T] Let $$\mathbf{ \text{F} } = \left( {e^{x}\sin y} \right)\mathbf{ \text{i} } + \left( {e^{x}\cos y} \right)\mathbf{ \text{j} } + z^{2}\mathbf{ \text{k} }.$$ Evaluate the integral $${\int_{C}{\mathbf{ \text{F} } \cdot d\mathbf{r}}},$$ where $$C$$ is the curve $${\mathbf{r}(t) = {< {\sqrt{t},t^{3},e^{\sqrt{t}}} >}},0 \leq t \leq 1.$$

[T] Let $$\mathbf{ \text{r} }:\left\lbrack {1,2} \right\rbrack\rightarrow\mathbb{R}^{2}$$ be given by $$x = e^{t - 1},y = \sin \left( \frac{\pi}{t} \right).$$ Use a computer to compute the integral $$\int_{C}{\mathbf{ \text{F} } \cdot d\mathbf{ \text{r} } = {\int_{C}{2x \cos ydx - x^{2}\sin ydy,}}}$$ where $$\mathbf{ \text{F} } = \left( {2x \cos y} \right)\mathbf{ \text{i} } - \left( {x^{2}\sin y} \right)\mathbf{ \text{j} }.$$

solution.paragraph: $$\int C F \cdot d r \approx 2 . 9923 \int C F \cdot d r \approx 2 . 9923$$

problem.paragraph: [T] Use a computer algebra system to find the mass of a wire that lies along curve $$\mathbf{ \text{r} }(t) = \left( {t^{2} - 1} \right)\mathbf{ \text{j} } + 2t\mathbf{ \text{k} },0 \leq t \leq 1,$$ if the density is $$\frac{3}{2}t.$$

Find the circulation and flux of field $$\mathbf{ \text{F} } = -y\mathbf{ \text{i} } + x\mathbf{ \text{j} }$$ around and across the closed semicircular path that consists of semicircular arch $$\mathbf{ \text{r} }_{1}(t) = \left( {a\cos t} \right)\mathbf{ \text{i} } + \left( {a\sin t} \right)\mathbf{ \text{j} },0 \leq t \leq \pi,$$ followed by line segment $$\mathbf{ \text{r} }_{2}(t) = t\mathbf{ \text{i} },-a \leq t \leq a.$$

solution.paragraph: $$circulation = \pi a 2 and flux = 0 circulation = \pi a 2 and flux = 0$$

problem.paragraph: Compute $${\int_{C}{\cos x \cos ydx - \sin x \sin ydy}},$$ where $$\textbf{c}(t) = {< {t,t^{2}} >},0 \leq t \leq 1.$$
Complete the proof of The Path Independence Test for Conservative Fields by showing that $$f_{y} = Q\left( {x,y} \right).$$
